0.0.n: 大蛇 is the first part of the name 大蛇丸; its characters mean giant snake.

0.1.n: 丸 completes the name 大蛇丸; it is not a separate word here.

0.2.n: は marks Orochimaru as the topic: the person this sentence is about.

0.4.n: 大きな directly describes the noun 蛇; this form must come before a noun.

0.5.n: Japanese nouns do not normally distinguish singular from plural, so 蛇 can mean one snake or several.

0.6.n: を marks 蛇 as what is summoned by 呼ぶ.

0.7.n: The plain form 呼ぶ describes 術 directly: a technique that summons snakes.

0.8.n: 術 refers to a special ninja technique here and is described by 大きな蛇を呼ぶ.

0.9.n: を marks the whole summoning technique as what Orochimaru can use.

0.10.n: 使えます is the polite form of 使える, expressing ability; the Japanese is nonpast, not past.

1.1.n: お前 is a rough, very familiar way to address someone and can sound insulting.

1.2.n: たち makes お前 refer to a group being addressed.

1.3.n: に marks the opponents someone might lose to with 負ける.

1.4.n: は adds contrast to に, singling out this group as opponents the speaker will not lose to.

1.5.n: 負けない is the plain negative form of 負ける, expressing a firm refusal or prediction here.

1.6.n: ぞ adds force and determination, with a rough, typically masculine tone.

2.0.n: 大蛇 begins the name 大蛇丸; do not read it as a separate snake here.

2.1.n: 丸 is the final part of the character's name 大蛇丸.

2.2.n: が identifies Orochimaru as the person raising his hand.

2.3.n: 手 refers to Orochimaru's hand; Japanese leaves the owner unstated when context makes it clear.

2.4.n: を marks 手 as what Orochimaru raises.

2.5.n: 上げる is in plain nonpast form before と, even though the sentence describes a past event.

2.6.n: と links the hand-raising to the event that immediately follows.

2.8.n: 大きな modifies 蛇 directly and is used only before a noun.

2.9.n: 蛇 names the creature appearing; Japanese does not add an equivalent of a here.

2.10.n: が marks 大きな蛇 as the creature that appears.

2.11.n: 現れました is the polite past form of 現れる, describing the snake coming into view.

0.lit: As for Orochimaru, he can use a technique that summons large snakes.
0.tip: 大きな蛇を呼ぶ comes before 術 to describe what the technique does.

1.lit: To you all, I will not lose!
1.tip: には highlights these particular opponents, strengthening the defiant claim.

2.lit: Orochimaru raised his hand, and when he did, a large snake appeared.
2.tip: A plain nonpast verb plus と can introduce a past event's trigger; the final verb supplies the past tense.
